ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, an inclined plane body c with inclination angle $\theta $ is placed on horizontal ground, a small box b is placed on the inclined plane, and it is connected to object a by a light string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The section of the light string connected to b is parallel to the inclined plane. The section of the light string connected to a is vertical. A is connected to a spring vertically fixed to the ground. Now an appropriate amount of sand grains is slowly put into box b, and abc always remains at rest. Which of the following statements is correct? (　　)
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: The friction force exerted by b on c may first decrease and then increase

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, an inclined plane body c with inclination angle $\theta$ is placed on horizontal ground, a small box b is placed on the inclined plane, and it is connected to object a by a light string passing over a smooth fixed pulley. The section of the light string connected to b is parallel to the inclined plane, and the section of the light string connected to a is vertical. a is connected to a spring vertically fixed to the ground. Now an appropriate amount of sand grains is slowly put into box b, and abc always remains at rest. How may the friction force exerted by b on c change?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The friction force exerted by b on c may first decrease and then increase
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the inclined plane body c is placed on horizontal ground, and the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal plane is marked as θ; the small box b is located on the inclined plane; a light string connects b along the direction of the inclined plane and passes over a smooth fixed pulley near the top of the inclined plane; the other end of the string is vertically downward and connected to object a; below a there is also a vertical spring connected, and the spring is fixed to the ground. Then reason: For b and the sand grains in the box as a whole, let the total mass be M. Along the direction of the inclined plane, it is subjected to the tension T of the string upward, the component Mg sinθ of gravity along the inclined plane downward, and the direction of the static friction force is determined by the relative magnitudes of the two. Analyze a in the vertical direction. Since a is always at rest and its position does not change, the deformation amount of the spring does not change, so the spring force does not change, and the gravity of a also does not change; therefore the tension T in the string is a constant. For b, write equilibrium along the inclined plane, and the magnitude of the static friction force is |Mg sinθ − T|. When sand is slowly added into b, M gradually increases, so Mg sinθ gradually increases, while T remains unchanged. If initially T > Mg sinθ, then the friction force first decreases as the difference between the two decreases; when Mg sinθ = T, the friction force can be zero; after continuing to add sand, Mg sinθ > T, and the friction force reverses direction and gradually increases. From action and reaction, it can be known that the magnitude of the friction force exerted by b on c may also first decrease and then increase, and its direction changes midway.
